rationale: Stem asks which listed precondition was NOT part of the Reconstruction Act of 1867 — a recall/identification question about a specific historical development, so 1.A (identify a historical concept, development, or process). Content is Congressional Reconstruction readmission policy, topic 5.10 Reconstruction (unit 5 matches period U5).

Stem asks why machines like Tammany Hall were successful 'primarily because' — it asks for an explanation of a historical development (the rise of political machines), so 1.B (explain a historical concept, development, or process). Content is urban machine politics, topic 6.13 Politics in the Gilded Age (unit 6 matches period U6).

Stem asks which listed factor(s) the 1929 stock market crash 'was the result of' — identifying the cause(s) of a historical development, so 1.A. The crash-to-Depression content is topic 7.9 The Great Depression (unit 7 matches period U7).

Stem asks which statement does NOT accurately describe the 1968 presidential election — identifying accurate descriptions of a historical development, so 1.A. The 1968 election (Democratic fracture over Vietnam, RFK assassination, Wallace third-party bid) is covered in the CED under topic 8.14 Society in Transition (unit 8 matches period U8).

Stem asks what Reagan pledged in the Reagan Doctrine (like Truman) — identifying the content of a foreign-policy doctrine, a historical development, so 1.A. Reagan's Cold War-era foreign policy sits under topic 9.2 Reagan and Conservatism (unit 9 matches period U9).

The 1848 Gerrit Smith quote advocates women's equal suffrage; the stem asks which trend the expressed sentiment matches — identifying the historical development consistent with the source, so 1.A. The women's-rights movement born in 1848 (Seneca Falls) is covered under topic 4.11 An Age of Reform (unit 4 matches period U4). Note: the stem frames the answer as a 'late 19th century' trend, so the suffrage campaign's later history extends into Periods 6/7, but the sentiment being judged is the 1848 origin.

Roger Williams's 1652 text criticizes civil power imposing religion — the task is identifying the criticized group (Puritans/established New England churches) and where they settled, so 1.A (identify a historical concept, development, or process). Puritan settlement patterns belong to topic 2.3 The Regions of British Colonies (unit 2 matches period U2).
